name: Kaida Fabrication Multi-Tool Wristband
description:
A heavy wristband with integrated fold-out tools — wire cutters, a flat-head driver, a bottle opener, a glass breaker, and a 5cm serrated blade. The tools nest flush into the band's surface and are invisible when stowed. The band itself is brushed titanium over a comfort liner.

Carried by mechanics, maintenance workers, and anyone who finds themselves regularly needing tools they don't have. The wristband's low profile means it passes most security checkpoints as jewelry — the serrated blade is the reason some checkpoints have upgraded their scanners.
functionality: Integrated multi-tool, covert blade, daily-carry utility
what_it_says: You solve small problems with your wrist and you've occasionally solved bigger problems with that blade.
story_hooks: A security checkpoint confiscates a Multi-Tool Wristband and discovers the serrated blade has been replaced with something that looks identical but is made from a material hard enough to cut through reinforced glass.

physical_description.visual_profile: A substantial, utilitarian wristband that reads as industrial jewelry—sits flush against the wrist with a minimalist aesthetic despite its functional density. Projects quiet competence and hands-on pragmatism. The brushed surface catches light subtly, appearing sophisticated rather than crude.
physical_description.fit: Snug but not restrictive, engineered for comfort during extended wear. Contours to the wrist without gaps, secured via friction-fit magnetic clasp that's nearly invisible when closed.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium outer shell over soft synthetic comfort liner (likely a pressure-responsive gel blend for sweat management and impact absorption).
physical_description.texture: The titanium exhibits a matte, directional grain from brushing—refined but deliberately un-polished. The edges are beveled smoothly. Tool seams are nearly imperceptible when flush; you feel them only as slight topographic variations under fingertips.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray titanium with black comfort liner visible only at the inner wrist edge. Minimal branding—Kaida Fabrication mark subtly etched on one edge.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap mechanism integrated into the titanium band. Silent, tool-accessible, and security-checkpoint-ambiguous by design.
distinctive_features: Five fold-out tools nested flush into the band surface: wire cutters, flat-head driver, bottle opener, glass breaker, 5cm serrated blade
Tools deploy via indexed pressure points—quiet, deliberate mechanical action
Serrated blade edge is why upgraded security scanners now flag the device
Comfort liner inner surface designed for sustained wear without chafing
Weight distributed to feel substantial without unbalancing the wrist
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3—working class tool, affordable but quality-engineered. Not aspirational, but respected. Second-hand market strong in sub-districts.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by maintenance workers, field mechanics, salvage operators, and anyone in the GLMZ who works with their hands. Signals practical self-sufficiency and trade competence. In corpo zones, sometimes worn ironically by lower-tier techs; in Tier 5 ungoverned sectors, considered essential kit.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and patina'd with use—the titanium develops a deeper matte finish from handling, minor scratches around tool access points, the comfort liner may show compression marks. Owner marks and modifications common (notches, scratches, personal symbols).
